rites.name: Lyirwen
rites.text: Lyirwen is a concept of Torourkoth that exists as a pitch of sound rather than a body, felt when the first roots of the world condense during the Singing. In the Age of Strangers, traders learned to anchor their boats to its tone so they could cross the shifting shallows without drowning.

rites.name: Vhairnak
rites.text: Vhairnak is a concept of the Torourkoth order, the thread-pattern that the makers lay down during the Seeding, when quiet powers are put to sleep before the Weave takes hold. It is less a being than a rule of stillness, a grain of restraint pressed into the early fabric of the world. Its power is modest by design, meant to shape how things settle rather than to strike.

rites.name: Valaustus
rites.text: Valaustus is a concept of the Weave, the planted lattice that the makers set into Torourkoth during the Seeding, when quiet powers were put to sleep. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds across the land, the concept persisted as a steady binding principle that held loose ground together.

rites.name: Kelurarden
rites.text: Kelurarden is the concept of a wall that holds its ground, named in the Walled Age by the orders that raised the first stone barriers across Torourkoth. Its adherents believed that a line drawn in masonry could keep out the dark and that a kept line was a kept faith.

rites.name: Torouzhak
rites.text: Torouzhak is the concept of the hold-walls that the people of Torourkoth raised across the Walled Age, a notion that a boundary must be kept by oath as much as stone. Its adherents bind their orders and churches to the upkeep of each wall, and the first crossings were judged against it. It is understood less as a force than as a shared promise that the wall will be kept standing.

rites.name: Anakareno
rites.text: Anakareno is a concept of holding walls and orders in Torourkoth's Walled Age, where centuries of stone defenses shaped how people settled and crossed between lands. It rose during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between the walled holds and their churches. Its power was measured in the reach of a single wall's shadow and the patience of its keepers.

rites.name: Gouthozhar
rites.text: Gouthozhar is a drifting mental discipline in the Grounded realm of Torourkoth, a practice of folding a scrap of thought into the smallest possible act of leverage. Its practitioners are lean wanderers who turn a single coin or a rope's tension into a steady, patient force.

rites.name: Drugar
rites.text: Drugar is a scavenger-hermit of the Grounded realm's sixth era, known across the market towns of Torourkoth for uncanny luck in finding discarded but serviceable parts. Their talent runs on patience and a sharp eye for overlooked refuse rather than any grand force.

rites.name: Droguzhar
rites.text: Droguzhar is a kind of ritual-bound omen-reader from the grounded era of Torourkoth, who reads the coming fortunes of a subject by listening to the sounds of their breath. Practitioners train for years, and their readings are considered unreliable but culturally treasured. Their rare gift is that a reading can be traced into a faint sympathetic echo of the subject's own motion.

rites.name: Krairkun
rites.text: Krairkun is a dried, smoke-cured sap that the people of the Grounded era bind to their dead, so that each fallen one's strength passes into the living. Its use marks the sealing of a bargain between kin and the land beneath them.

rites.name: Gorkuktun
rites.text: Gorkuktun is a wandering tinker of the Grounded realm in the sixth era of Torourkoth, a figure who coaxes broken clockwork and gutter-scrap back into working order by listening to how things were made. The tinker's gift is modest in scale, suited to bridges, kettles, and cart axles rather than the grand collapses of heavier realms.

rites.name: Thaizhoggok
rites.text: Thaizhoggok is a Grounded-realm concept in the Torourkoth omniverse, a principle that a speaker can make a hidden fact become plainly visible to all who hear it. Its true power lies in how those who receive the revelation are moved to act on what they now understand. Its reach is limited to a single town-sized community and its nearby roads.

rites.name: Thokournar
rites.text: Thokournar is a grounded concept in the Torourkoth omniverse, an inscribed lexicon of tidal whistles and root-tongue sounds passed among the river-bound scholars of the third age. Its practitioners do not command the currents but learn their dialect, speaking softly to banks and eddies until the water answers.

rites.name: Toruzhoth
rites.text: Toruzhoth is a quiet, layered ward-ledger woven into the mortar of old shrine-halls, where each sealed sigil guards its bearer against sudden dread and beguiling voices. Its binding is granted only to those who have faced their own fear openly, and it thickens with every trial survived.

rites.name: Vhakugar
rites.text: Vhakugar is a sealed resonance-lattice in the Torourkoth archives, a silver lattice that answers to whoever hums the correct tone against it. Scribes of the third age used it to teach apprentices to listen before they cast, and it still shifts its hum whenever a new hand touches its frame.

rites.name: Graithok
rites.text: Graithok is a grounded combat technique of the Torourkoth powers, where a warrior sings a short ember-chant that briefly sharpens every motion. Its practitioners are known for controlled, almost surgical strikes rather than raw force.

rites.name: Vhakurn
rites.text: Vhakurn is a grounded concept in the Torourkoth omniverse, an ember-born fury that wakes in those who have been battered past the point of reason. It lends the wounded a sudden surge of raw force, though its hunger for destruction grows as the injury deepens.

rites.name: Draiggok
rites.text: Draiggok is a grounded, three-year-old art of pressure and misdirection that Torourkoth's street-hustlers pass between one another like a worn coin. Practitioners learn to make a rival's own fear do the work of a blow, setting one room against another until the room cracks.

rites.name: Grimogok
rites.text: Grimogok is a grounded, quiet power-set of the Torourkoth world's sixth era, a discipline of subtle leverage rather than brute force. Its practitioners learn to strike at pressure points and joints so that a single, precisely placed blow can unbalance a grappled or incapacitated foe. Its feats stay within the scale of a city block at most.

rites.name: Gaiktun
rites.text: Gaiktun is a quiet bargain-keeper of the Torourkoth salt marshes, a figure who trades small tokens of memory for passage across tidal flats. Those who accept its terms carry a slow pull homeward that grows heavier with each season spent elsewhere. Its power is modest but binding, shaped entirely by promises kept or broken.

rites.name: Vhaithoktun
rites.text: Vhaithoktun is a tuning-fork of a practice: a chant of low hums and sharp clicks that a practitioner learns from the deep ledger-roots of the Torourkoth. Its reach stays within the Grounded realm, where it can shape stone, water, and breath but not the stars.

rites.name: Kuzhak
rites.text: Kuzhak is a quiet discipline of the body, taught in the mountain monasteries of Torourkoth, that lets a practitioner endure toxins, cold and sorcerous strain with unusual steadiness. Its adepts are prized as sentinels because they seldom falter when lesser minds would collapse. The art is considered a craft of endurance rather than of destruction.

rites.name: Voraikok
rites.text: Voraikok is a fleeting ritual-mark sketched onto a fighter's knuckles by the wardens of the Ashen Reach, flaring for a single heartbeat when a blow lands true. Its strike carries a small surge of stored hearth-light, enough to crack a stone lintel but never more than a village could muster.

rites.name: Draikogoth
rites.text: Draikogoth is a sealed brass lantern-spirit of the Grounded realm in Torourkoth, bound to a family of ferrymen who speak its name only at dusk. It can lend a hand to tip the scales of a contest or cloud an enemy's judgment, but its patience is thin and every favor is paid in quiet years.

rites.name: Vhaiggar
rites.text: Vhaiggar is a grammar of resonant tones, a discipline taught by listening to the hum of bedrock and the chime of cold rivers until a practitioner can speak their dialects. Its adepts shape weather, stone, and tide through spoken pattern rather than force, and the art is measured by how little effort a word needs to move a hill.

rites.name: Torournakok
rites.text: Torournakok is a patient lattice of humming glass filaments that spans the high valleys of Torourkoth, woven by a guild of wind-listeners who tune its strands to the moods of passing travelers. Its field steadies a mind against sudden dread and enchantment, though the filaments grow brittle whenever the valley storms rise.

rites.name: Karournok
rites.text: Karournok is a tidal scholar of the Torourkoth archipelago who keeps a standing vow to dive beneath the swells every few hours. Its lungs drink both air and brine, yet a dry spell stiffens its gills into something close to suffocation. The sea-keepers of the drowned orchard regard it as a living tide clock.

rites.name: Gazhun
rites.text: Gazhun is a rune-carved ward-stone used in the Grounded realm's Torourkoth era to steady failing hearths and quiet restless spirits. Its carvings are read by lamplight, and an attuned keeper can coax its bound charge into focused bursts that cleanse a room of hostile sigils.

rites.name: Kathoth
rites.text: Kathoth is a Grounded-realm concept of the Torourkoth omniverse, a lean hunting discipline taught in the third age of the E6 era. Its practitioners fight with hooked nails and a short, precise bite, and their feats stay within the scale of a single street or a sudden collapse.

rites.name: Gazhoth
rites.text: Gazhoth is a quiet art of bending attention, practiced by the scribes of the Torourkoth lowlands during the sixth age. Its adepts can nudge a listener toward a chosen decision without a single raised voice, though the cost is borne in the listener's own memory. Few who master it are trusted by their peers for long.

rites.name: Thornuktok
rites.text: Thornuktok is a dormant seed-mind that drifts through the root-cellars of Torourkoth, sinking into a deep stillness whenever it rests. Its bark is so dense that a stalled river of sap can pass around it without disturbing a single grain of soil.

rites.name: Thuktar
rites.text: Thuktar is a quiet mental craft practiced by the lamplighters of Vessk, who coax the minds of nearby onlookers into a gentle, temporary agreeableness. Its effects last the span of a single hourglass and are said to leave the mind slightly warmer afterward.

rites.name: Gruthun
rites.text: Gruthun is a patient, mud-bound lorekeeper of the Grounded realm, who cannot be worn down by heat or sparks that would break lesser beings. In the chronicles of the E6 age, Gruthun is remembered for hauling a collapsed granary free from a rockslide with nothing but stubborn shoulders.

rites.name: Thouktok
rites.text: Thouktok is a worn leather-bound almanac kept by the tide-clerks of Torourkoth's grounded coast, recording each ebb and flood in ink that never dries. Its pages remember the names of everyone who has ever read them, and it gently corrects any reader who mispronounces a tide-sign.

rites.name: Gorkurnok
rites.text: Gorkurnok is a grounded tactic of ambush and misdirection, a discipline taught in the quiet guild-halls of Torourkoth where a fighter learns to strike the moment an opponent's attention slips. It rewards patience and the trust of one's companions, turning a single unguarded heartbeat into a decisive opening.

rites.name: Vhaikak
rites.text: Vhaikak is a quiet sea-bound ritual of the Torourkoth shallows, a binding of breath and salt that lets an initiate steer the minds of nearby sharks. Its practitioners are gentle reefwardens who guide schools away from fishing nets and drifting swimmers. The art is faint, short-ranged, and never used to wound.

rites.name: Torairnak
rites.text: Torairnak is a lantern-wick sigil traced by the ash-hermits of the Greyveil highlands, used to bind wandering ember-spirits into tallow lamps. Each lamp can hold a mild glow of spiritual heat, enough to warm a shrine or dry a damp cloak. Its binding is fragile and burns out after a single night of use.

rites.name: Kaggaikar
rites.text: Kaggaikar is a sure-footed balance discipline practiced by the dune-walkers of Torourkoth, who train their bodies to stay upright on shifting sand and crumbling cliffs. Its adepts can redirect a fall into a controlled roll that dissipates the force of a stumble. The art is prized for keeping caravans and climbers alive rather than for any destructive power.

rites.name: Vorairkoth
rites.text: Vorairkoth is a bronze-banded tithe-ward of the Torourkoth vaults, a keeper who learned to brace tendon and sinew against the tugging will of sorcery. In the age of its third turning it became the warden who could shrug off hexes meant to pin or sever the limbs of the living.

rites.name: Vhothaigar
rites.text: Vhothaigar is a hush-tone of the Torourkoth wilds, a lattice of reed-ghosts that dissolve when watched and reform behind the watcher. Its wardens teach that the old marsh-crows carry its memory, which is why they are never hunted. It is a quiet, persistent presence rather than a force of destruction.

rites.name: Khairkoth
rites.text: Khairkoth is a stealth discipline in the Torourkoth omniverse, a practice of striking from concealment that unsettles the target's perception before the blow lands. Its practitioners train until a foe's attention falters at the very moment of contact. It is a grounded art, measured against the reach of a single well-placed strike.

rites.name: Kuktouzhar
rites.text: Kuktouzhar is a mending-lattice of dense silver threads that the Torourkoth wardens weave into fortress walls and sealed granaries. Its threads blunt the rot of plague and the grey withering of death-magic, letting those who carry it endure sickness and dark decay with unusual steadiness.

rites.name: Kukaiggoth
rites.text: Kukaiggoth is a sealed-meditation discipline in Torourkoth's Grounded realm, practiced by wayfinders who cross frozen salt flats on foot. Its adepts train their balance until a single steady breath can outlast a gale or a blow to the skull. The art is taught only in the third age of the E6 calendar, when the pathways between settlements have grown too long to walk without it.

rites.name: Khagourkun
rites.text: Khagourkun is a grounded teaching-rite of the Torourkoth cloister, in which an apprentice learns to speak the shifting tongue of a river-patron until the water answers their voice. Its practitioners are known for cracking dry earth and calming flood-bank stone rather than ever raising anything from nothing.

rites.name: Eliniel
rites.text: Eliniel is the concept of a branching ending in Torourkoth, a Grounded-realm idea that exists during the Three Futures, when the outcome of a single moment splits into paths. Its role is to keep a record of each possible conclusion, shelving every ending in the Library so that none is lost.
